definitions.note: a cryptic description: fish are taken from the blue sea

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: fish are hauled up from the sea, poetically the deep blue
second meaning: the idiom for something arriving without warning

explanation.surface: An angler explains how fish get caught.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish really are taken from the blue sea, and the same phrase is an idiom for something arriving without warning.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something arriving suddenly with no warning, like a bolt from a clear sky.

blocks.note: a number that is not even is odd
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A card that marks a dance as not yet over, perhaps a dance card at a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: A card is an old-fashioned word for an eccentric or comic person, which the dance card of the surface hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a card means they are a comic, eccentric character, exactly what an oddball is.

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
wee is Scots for small

explanation.surface: A spectator snatches a quick look in the middle of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT races are motorcycle races held on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A peep is the small chirping sound of a young bird, also called a tweet.

clue.text: If upset, army commander becomes what Walton was

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the short word is read from the bottom

blocks.note: taken as written before being turned
William Tecumseh Sherman, Union general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: If a general is disturbed, he turns into what a historical figure was.
explanation.walkthrough: Izaak Walton wrote The Compleat Angler, the classic 17th-century book on fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Izaak Walton was a famous angler, author of The Compleat Angler, so he was one who catches fish.

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the name from the bottom of the column to the top

blocks.note: Winnie-the-Pooh, A. A. Milne's bear

explanation.surface: An instruction to telephone someone called Winnie.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring looks like a verb meaning phone; it is the noun for a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoop is a circular band, so it is a ring shape.

blocks.note: a band is a group of musicians
taken as written
a judge hears a case, that is, tries it

explanation.surface: Someone reports hearing that some musicians were hijacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hear' looks like a sound-alike signal, but it is plain wordplay: hear in the courtroom sense of try a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Hijacking is robbery by force, the kind of lawless crime carried out by bandits.

blocks.note: first meaning: your dad's brother
second meaning: old slang for a pawnbroker, with whom you pop (pawn) your goods

explanation.surface: A family note about dad's brother and visiting him.
explanation.walkthrough: To pop something is British slang for pawning it, and the pawnbroker was nicknamed by the same family word as dad's brother.
explanation.definitionFit: A father's brother is this relative, and old slang gave the same name to a pawnbroker.

clue.text: Love music? Not against broadcast from stadium

indicators.note: the clue asks us to leave out the letter that stands for against, as in a sports fixture
broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
v for versus, as in Arsenal v Spurs

explanation.surface: A music lover who won't be put off hearing a concert broadcast from a stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: V for versus is removed from the first two words before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Coliseum, or Colosseum, is the great amphitheatre of Rome, and the word is used for any large arena.

indicators.note: a rumour passes by word of mouth, so the word wanted is one heard rather than seen

blocks.note: someone ailing is doing feebly

explanation.surface: Gossip that a magazine is in financial trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A periodical published every seven days is called by this name, as in a news magazine.

definitions.note: a cryptic description: a dressing put down, like a floor covering

blocks.note: first meaning: to carpet someone is to scold them
second meaning, read whimsically: a covering, or dressing, laid down on the boards

explanation.surface: A rug laid over the floorboards.
explanation.walkthrough: To carpet someone is to summon them for a telling-off; a carpet on the floor is also a dressing laid down.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carpeted means being reprimanded by a superior, which is the same as a stern scolding.

blocks.note: first meaning: nearby, not far away
second meaning: the finish or conclusion of something

explanation.surface: Something is about to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelt the same, one word is an adjective for nearby and a noun for a finish, said differently.

clue.text: The man composed music for a choir

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer wrote a piece for a choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' fits the musical surface perfectly while signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a choral setting of a sacred text sung in church services.

blocks.note: a side is a team in sport
a kick is a thrill, as in getting a kick out of something

explanation.surface: Linking a sports team with thrills.
explanation.walkthrough: Associate looks like a verb; it is the noun for a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is a close companion or assistant, the partner of a hero.

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

blocks.note: Robert E. Lee, Confederate general
a gum is a chewy sweet

explanation.surface: A general remark that fruit is sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' reads as 'generally'; here general is a person with a sweet inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically, a pea or bean pod is a fruit, and such pods are called legumes.

indicators.note: something slippery slides about, so the letters slither out of order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Walking on a slippery hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is the steepness of an incline, and by extension the incline itself.

clue.text: China - in its capital, a place designed for plant-growing

indicators.note: a capital letter is the one standing at the head of a word, so only the opener is kept

blocks.note: its refers back to the word China
a garden bed of rocks with alpine plants among them

explanation.surface: A note about China, its capital city and a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its capital' looks like Beijing; it means the capital letter of China.
explanation.definitionFit: China is fine porcelain tableware, and plates and cups in general are crockery.

blocks.note: first meaning: one who wins
second meaning: William I, who won the English throne in 1066

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like first names; only William is a name here.
explanation.definitionFit: A victor defeats an enemy, and William of Normandy carries that title after Hastings in 1066.

indicators.note: scattered grain is thrown about, so the letters fall in a new order
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written
every one is each one

explanation.surface: Grain spilled along every ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: Trench looks like a noun for a ditch; as a verb, to trench on means to intrude on.
explanation.definitionFit: To trench on or upon something is an old verb meaning to intrude on territory or rights.

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

blocks.note: the opening letter of teachers
showering, as in raining gifts on someone

explanation.surface: A head teacher generously providing schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Training is instruction in a skill, a form of teaching and learning.

clue.text: Fight - caught us sleeping in the middle

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit in the middle of the words that follow, straddling them

blocks.note: spans the end of caught, all of us and the start of sleeping

explanation.surface: A fight broke out and caught us napping halfway through.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a vigorous scuffle or struggle, a minor fight.

clue.text: Hate a rain-cloud that's not black

indicators.note: the clue asks for the letter that stands for black to be dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
a nimbus is a rain-bearing cloud
B for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes a grey rain-cloud that isn't fully dark.
explanation.walkthrough: B is the standard abbreviation for black.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is hostile feeling or ill will towards someone, a close synonym for hostility.

blocks.note: first meaning: firm, steadfast, loyal
second meaning: to stop a flow, as of blood from a wound

explanation.walkthrough: Stem looks like a plant's stalk; it is the verb meaning stop a flow, often spelt stanch.
explanation.definitionFit: A staunch supporter is firm and loyal, and to staunch bleeding is to stop it flowing.

definitions.note: read as slipper-y, having the nature of a slipper

blocks.note: first meaning: hard to pin down
second meaning, whimsically: a mule is a backless slipper, so like one is slipper-ish

explanation.surface: Someone dodging questions, stubborn as a mule.
explanation.walkthrough: A mule is the stubborn animal in the surface, but also a backless slipper; adding Y makes 'like a slipper'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slippery person is shifty and hard to pin down, never giving a straight answer.

clue.text: Cruise  ship's forward section beginning to leak

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: the prow is the front part of a ship's hull
the first letter of leak

explanation.surface: A cruise liner's bow starting to let in water.
explanation.walkthrough: Cruise suggests a holiday voyage; here it is the verb for moving about looking for prey.
explanation.definitionFit: To prowl is to move stealthily around an area, as a cruising predator or kerb-crawler does.

blocks.note: first meaning: the West African republic
second meaning: the old British gold coin worth 21 shillings

explanation.surface: A remark about a nation's currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The guinea, an old British coin worth one pound and one shilling, was named after the African gold region.
explanation.definitionFit: Guinea is a nation on the coast of West Africa and also a former British coin.

indicators.note: to metamorphose is to change form, so the letters take a new shape

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A myth in which the goddess Diana is transformed into a nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ovid-style surface fits: Diana is the Roman goddess of hunting, attended by nymphs.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a naiad is a water spirit living in springs, rivers and lakes, one kind of nymph.

indicators.note: a pair parted by something has it placed between them

blocks.note: South and North are partners at the bridge table
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A bridge pair broken up by dad.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge, North plays with South and East with West.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the stretch of a bridge between supports, and as a verb to span is to bridge.

clue.text: Nothing about to be accepted in jargon

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word before is read from right to left

blocks.note: nil is zero, nothing
if something goes, it is accepted, as in anything goes

explanation.surface: Nothing is about to be approved in technical language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of'; split it, and about turns the zero word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for the specialised vocabulary of a group, which is what jargon means.

clue.text: When somebody's written about one, it's libel

indicators.note: something written about another wraps round it

blocks.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
a somebody is a person
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: When someone has been written about, the article is defamatory.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspersion is a damaging, often false, remark about someone's reputation, close to a libel.

clue.text: Familiar number that's half a 16th century tune

blocks.note: surface reading: a well-known song
setter's reading: the hymn tune dates from 1551, halfway through that century, and its name is an old way of saying a numbered psalm

explanation.surface: A well-known song described as dating from the middle of Tudor times.
explanation.walkthrough: The tune was first printed in the Genevan Psalter of 1551, about half-way through the century; it is sung to 'All people that on earth do dwell', a version of Psalm 100.
explanation.definitionFit: This famous hymn tune takes its name from Psalm 100, whose metrical version it carries, and was published in 1551.
